Entry title: Indoor air can be dirtier than outside
Content: The EPA notes indoor air pollutant levels can be higher than outdoor levels. Controlling sources, airing out rooms and filtering air all help.
Source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
Label: Evidence summary - education only

Content: Blocked vents and unserviced systems reduce fresh air. Keep grilles clear and report stuffy rooms.
Source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
Label: Evidence summary - education only

Content: A 2024 study measured tiny plastic particles in home and car air. Regular dusting, vacuuming and ventilation reduce indoor dust.
Source: Human exposure to PM10 microplastics in indoor air - PLOS One
Label: Evidence summary - education only

Content: New furniture, paint and cleaners can release chemicals (VOCs) indoors. Choose low-emission products and air out rooms after renovating.
Source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
Label: Evidence summary - education only
